item.text:
Turn complete. Report updated at [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-09_14-01-25-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md).

Three things this turn, the middle one being the substantive contribution.

I finished reading the two sensitive paths I hadn't fully covered: `RecoverCluster` (snapshot restore, log replay from `snapshotIndex+1`, snapshot-at-index-1 with the supplied configuration, then full log compaction) and `restoreUserSnapshot` (config-stability check, inflight cancellation, index burn `lastIndex++`, FSM restore with panic-on-failure, and `setLastLog`/`setLastApplied`/`setLastSnapshot`). Both canonical.

I then validated Finding 1 causally. In a scratch copy of the module I applied only the one-line fix and re-ran both flaky tests 20 times each under identical conditions:

| test | unmodified `work/` | fixed scratch copy |
|---|---|---|
| `TestRaft_ProtocolVersion_Upgrade_2_3` | 6/20 fail | 0/20 fail |
| `TestRaft_HasExistingState` | 4/20 fail | 0/20 fail |

So the single missing `peerSet = c.getConfiguration(c.rafts[0])` refresh is both necessary and sufficient for the flakiness — a clean root-cause confirmation rather than a correlation. The captured implementation was never modified: `diff -rq source work` still shows no differing files.

Finally, a hygiene fix: the scratch copy initially sat inside the module as `fixcheck/`, which would have appeared in `go test ./...` as a duplicate of the raft package. I moved it to `_scratch_fixcheck/` (Go ignores leading-underscore directories), confirmed `go list ./...` now shows only `raft`, `bench`, and my two `repro` tools, and that `go vet ./...` is clean. I also refreshed the report's status line, summary bullets, and the now-stale paths.

The audit's final state stands: one confirmed defect (Finding 1 in `testing.go`'s `EnsureSamePeers`, now causally validated), no consensus-level defect by source review plus five independent behavioral methods (~16k acked commands), and the single open question — whether the missing refresh line is the injected mutation or a latent upstream flake — unanswerable offline without a trustworthy upstream reference. Evidence is preserved durably in `work/audit-evidence/`.
